subtopics.title: India's solar position and records
subtopics.summary: According to IRENA Renewable Energy Statistics 2026, India added 37 GW of solar capacity in 2025 and became the world's second largest solar growth market. India overtook Japan to become the world's third largest solar power producer in 2025. The country also hosts Bhadla Solar Park, India's largest solar plant at 2245 MW, and Omkareshwar, India's largest floating solar plant at 600 MW.
facts: India added 37 GW of solar capacity in 2025 (IRENA Renewable Energy Statistics 2026)
India emerged as the world's 2nd largest solar growth market
China added 315 GW of solar in 2025 and remained the largest
Global solar capacity rose from 1880 GW in 2024 to 2392 GW in 2025
India overtook Japan to become the world's 3rd largest solar power producer in 2025
India ranked 3rd globally in total renewable energy installed capacity with 250.52 GW
Top solar states: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Maharashtra
Bhadla Solar Park (Jodhpur, Rajasthan, 2245 MW): India's largest solar plant
Omkareshwar (Khandwa, Madhya Pradesh, 600 MW): India's largest floating solar plant
Rajarhat (Kolkata): India's first floating solar plant (2015)

subtopics.title: Global initiatives and climate commitments
subtopics.summary: India's COP26 climate commitments, called Panchamrita, include net zero by 2070 and 500 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030. The Global Solar Facility, launched at COP27 in 2022, provides payment guarantees to de-risk solar investments. The OSOWOG concept, first proposed by India in 2018, advocates trans-national solar power connectivity through integrated regional grids.
facts: Panchamrita: India's climate commitments at COP26 in Glasgow
Net zero target by the year 2070
Non-fossil energy capacity of 500 GW by 2030
Meet 50 percent of energy requirements from renewable energy by 2030
Reduce total projected carbon emissions by one billion tonnes from now till 2030
Global Solar Facility launched at COP27 (2022) to provide payment guarantees and de-risk solar investments
STAR-C trains engineers, entrepreneurs and policymakers in solar technologies
One Sun, One World, One Grid (India and UK, COP26) advocates trans-national solar connectivity
India first proposed the OSOWOG concept in 2018 during ISA's Inaugural Assembly
OSOWOG aims to integrate regional grids across Asia, Middle East, Africa and Europe for 24-hour renewable power
